content.rendered:
Let’s learn, grow and share together.

As a community partner, we want all members of the community to succeed. We’re proud to offer you many options to educate yourself on the topics most important to you, as you work to meet your financial and career goals. We encourage you to share these resources with anyone you feel would benefit from attending a class or viewing our complimentary materials.

As part of Averon Trust Bank’s commitment to community education, we’ve partnered with CVENT to provide online scheduling and registration services. By clicking on a class, you will be redirected to the registration website hosted by CVENT. CVENT has agreed not to share the information you enter on your registration with anyone other than Averon Trust Bank. CVENT will only use the information it collects from your registration for scheduling you for class and sending information related to that class.

Home

Do you want homeownership to be in your future? Join us to start Budgeting, understanding the Power of Credit, preparing to be a First Time Home Buyer, and more.

Attend our classes before making that big purchase


Don’t see a class you need right now? Check out our on-demand content on YouTube.

Or check out these resources (and many others) at our Learning Hub:

  • Buying a Home and Understanding Mortgages
  • Understanding Credit Reports and Scores
  • Creating a Budget (and sticking to it)

Youth

Looking for fun, educational content to share with your kids outside of the usual school curriculum? Check out our Online Learning Shakeup program that combines literature, math, art and personal finance into an exciting hour long class, or the Kids STEAM Summer Series. Register today for classes that will teach kids useful life skills while engaging in exciting, interactive learning.

Register today for our youth classes


Or check out these resources (and many others) at our Learning Hub:

  • Financial Football
  • GPS to Success: Find out What Different Careers are About
  • How to Teach Your Kids the Value of Saving
  • Financial Education for Grades Prek-2
  • Financial Education for Grades 3-5
  • Financial Education for 6-8

Teens

If your teen just landed his or her first job, having a place to put earnings and understanding when to spend and how to save is important. We currently offer Forte U Student Banking: Starting Out and Forte U Student Banking: Financial Adulting, where we’ll go over all the financial basics, including how to use a debit card, save for a goal, and the ins and outs of earning good credit.

Sign Up for Classes Geared at Teens Today


Or check out these resources (and many others) at our Learning Hub and Averon Trust YouTube Channel:

  • Borrowing Smart and Paying for Higher Education
  • Scholarship Search Tool
  • Staying on Track with Student Loans while You Are in School
  • Buying or Leasing a Car  
  • Banking with Financial Institutions
  • Financial Education for High School

Family Life

Juggling how to pay the mortgage while saving for your kid’s education, your parent’s medical care and your own retirement is a huge challenge! Let us help guide you and answer your questions during our live classes on Budgeting, Paying for College, Teaching from Home Tips from a Teacher, a panel discussion to determine Are You Ready to Be Your Parent’s Caregiver, and more.

Check out our upcoming classes on family life


Or check out these resources (and many others) at our Learning Hub:

  • Setting Up an Emergency Fund
  • Saving for a Child’s Education
  • Scholarship Search Tool
  • When is it Time To Take Over Your Parent’s Finances

Marriage and Partnership

Are you beginning to build your future with someone special? Many big discussions on your priorities and how to spend money are in your future. Register for classes about becoming a First Time Home Buyer, Budgeting for a Wedding, and more. 

Say “I DO” to learning more


Or check out these resources (and many others) at our Learning Hub:

  • Real Talk: Financial Considerations When Getting Married 
  • Everything You Need to Know About Financially Preparing for a Wedding 
  • Creating a Budget and Sticking to It
  • Married Filing Jointly/Separately, Head of Household: What Are These and Why It Matters
  • Cheers to 30 Years: 8 Tips for Managing Your Finances in Your Thirties

Think Like an Entrepreneur

Want to be more innovative and entrepreneurial?  You don’t have to start your own business to think like an entrepreneur – the benefits to you and your organization are increased innovation, creativity, and goal attainment. Register to join a Business Book Club, hone your Public Speaking skills, or improve Time Management, and more.

View Upcoming Classes and Register


Or check out these resources (and many others) at our Learning Hub:

  • How to Maximize Your Earning Potential and Develop Your Career
  • How to Enhance Your Value at Work
  • How Self-Assessment Can Help Your Career

Career

Starting out in your career? Or been in your job for a while but know there are areas where you want to do better? Join us online to improve your Public Speaking skills, to learn about Checking and Savings Accounts and becoming Financially Fit now that you are earning a regular paycheck, and more.

Check out upcoming classes and register


Or check out these resources (and many others) at our Learning Hub:

  • Understanding Your Paycheck and W2’s
  • Maximizing Your Career Potential and Developing Your Career
  • Six Soft Skills that Can Help Advance Your Career

Retirement

While many people look forward to the stress of work and busy schedules being behind them, preparing for retirement can be stressful too as you consider how you want to spend your time, income stream, and planned and unplanned expenses. Join us for classes and conversation on Social Security, Medicare, IRA Bootcamp, ID Theft for Older Adults, and other topics that will help you properly prepare for your future. 

Join us for classes and conversations about retirement


Or check out these resources (and many others) at our Learning Hub:

  • Protecting Yourself from Identity Theft and Scams
  • Creating a Financial Plan for Your Proprieties and Goals
  • Social Security 

Senior Life

We want you to enjoy your golden years. To do so, it’s important to have your budget for the life you live today, plans in place if you (or your partner) pass away, an awareness of the many identity theft and financial scams used to prey on older adults, and of course, opportunities to connect with your peers, kids and grandkids. Consider registering to talk Budgeting, ID Theft for Older Adults, How to Use Your Cell Phone, Estate Planning, or joining one of our Book Clubs. 

Check out our Senior Life Classes


Or check out these resources (and many others) at our Learning Hub:

  • Estate Planning: Specialized Trusts
  • Make a Budget that Meets Where You Are Now
  • Beware Identity Theft Scams on Your Cell Phone
